review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

3:1.sourceText: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς συναγωγήν, καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπος ἐξηραμμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα·
3:1.targetText: Once again Jesus entered the synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.

groups.note: εἰσῆλθεν εἰς, "went into", is rendered entered.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.
N1904 has no article before συναγωγήν; BSB's the matches the reading εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν.

3:2.sourceText: καὶ παρετήρουν αὐτὸν εἰ τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύσει αὐτόν, ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
3:2.targetText: In order to accuse Jesus, they were watching to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.

groups.note: αὐτοῦ, "him", is rendered with the name Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed; English begins with the purpose clause.
The object αὐτόν ("Him") of watching is not separately expressed; English refers to Him as the subject of would heal.
The object αὐτόν ("him", the man) of healing is left unexpressed in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb of seeing to introduce the indirect question with if.

3:3.sourceText: καὶ λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ τὴν χεῖρα ἔχοντι ξηράν Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον.
3:3.targetText: Then Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up among us.”

groups.note: The article τῷ with the participle ἔχοντι, "the one having", is rendered with.
εἰς τὸ μέσον, "into the middle", is rendered among us.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker that the Greek verb ending implies.

3:4.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν ἀγαθὸν ποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀποκτεῖναι; οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων.
3:4.targetText: And He asked them, “Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”  But they were silent.

groups.note: ψυχήν is the object of both infinitives; English repeats it as it.
In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.

unmappedTarget.reason: English turns the either-or question into a which-question; the Greek has no interrogative word.

3:5.sourceText: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος αὐτοὺς μετ’ ὀργῆς, συνλυπούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ πωρώσει τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα. καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.
3:5.targetText: Jesus looked around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored.

groups.note: The verse-opening καί is rendered Then where BSB begins its second sentence.
The participle συνλυπούμενος, "being grieved", is rendered as the noun sorrow.
ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ, "his hand", is resumed in English as it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek participle implies.
English joins the participle συνλυπούμενος to anger as a second noun; no καί is printed.
English supplies the object of stretched that the Greek leaves understood.
N1904 has no σου after χεῖρα; BSB's your matches the reading τὴν χεῖρά σου.

3:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εὐθὺς μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν συμβούλιον ἐδίδουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ, ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
3:6.targetText: At this, the Pharisees went out and began plotting with the Herodians how they might kill Jesus.

groups.note: The opening καί is rendered At this, introducing the Pharisees' response.
συμβούλιον ἐδίδουν, "were giving counsel", is rendered began plotting.
αὐτόν, "him", is rendered with the name Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves εὐθύς ("immediately") unexpressed in this verse.
κατ’ αὐτοῦ ("against Him") is left implicit in the plot to kill Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἐξελθόντες is rendered as the finite verb went out.

3:7.sourceText: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀνεχώρησεν πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἠκολούθησεν· καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας
3:7.targetText: So Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, accompanied by a large crowd from Galilee, Judea,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts "and a large crowd … followed" as accompanied by, so this καί has no English word.
BSB lists Judea after Galilee with a comma; καὶ ἀπό ("and from") is covered by the one from.

3:8.sourceText: καὶ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰδουμαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου καὶ περὶ Τύρον καὶ Σιδῶνα, πλῆθος πολύ, ἀκούοντες ὅσα ποιεῖ, ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
3:8.targetText: Jerusalem, Idumea, the region beyond the Jordan, and the vicinity of Tyre and Sidon. The large crowd came to Him when they heard what great things He was doing.

groups.note: N1904 reads the present ποιεῖ (BSB's text ἐποίει); English reported speech puts either in the past.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the places with commas; the repeated καί and ἀπό ("and from") are covered by from in 3:7.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English resumes the crowd of 3:7 with a definite article; πλῆθος πολύ has none.

3:9.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα πλοιάριον προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον, ἵνα μὴ θλίβωσιν αὐτόν·
3:9.targetText: Jesus asked His disciples to have a boat ready for Him so that the crowd would not crush Him.

groups.note: προσκαρτερῇ, "should stand ready", is rendered have … ready.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB makes the crowd the subject of crush, so διά ("because of") has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker that the Greek verb ending implies.

3:10.sourceText: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐθεράπευσεν, ὥστε ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται ὅσοι εἶχον μάστιγας.
3:10.targetText: For He had healed so many that all who had diseases were pressing forward to touch Him.

groups.note: ὥστε, "so that", introduces the result; English places so before many.

unmappedSource.reason: The dative αὐτῷ ("on Him") of pressing is not separately expressed; English names Him once, as the one touched.

3:11.sourceText: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα, ὅταν αὐτὸν ἐθεώρουν, προσέπιπτον αὐτῷ καὶ ἔκραζον λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ.
3:11.targetText: And when the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down before Him and cried out, “You are the Son of God!”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB introduces the quotation without rendering λέγοντα ("saying") or the recitative ὅτι.

3:12.sourceText: καὶ πολλὰ ἐπετίμα αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ αὐτὸν φανερὸν ποιήσωσιν.
3:12.targetText: But He warned them sternly not to make Him known.

3:13.sourceText: Καὶ ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος, καὶ προσκαλεῖται οὓς ἤθελεν αὐτός, καὶ ἀπῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
3:13.targetText: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and called for those He wanted, and they came to Him.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

3:14.sourceText: καὶ ἐποίησεν δώδεκα ἵνα ὦσιν μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν
3:14.targetText: He appointed twelve of them, whom He designated as apostles, to accompany Him, to be sent out to preach,

groups.note: ὦσιν μετ’, "be with", is rendered accompany.
English turns "that He might send them out" into the passive be sent out.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB joins the two purpose clauses with a comma, so this καί has no English word.
With the passive be sent out, αὐτούς ("them") has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a partitive referring to those called in 3:13.
N1904 lacks οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν; BSB follows the reading that includes it.

3:15.sourceText: καὶ ἔχειν ἐξουσίαν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια·
3:15.targetText: and to have authority to drive out demons.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐποίησεν τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρον·
3:16.targetText: These are the twelve He appointed: Simon (whom He named Peter),

groups.note: ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα, "put a name on", is rendered named.

unmappedSource.reason: These καί are not separately expressed; English sets out the names as a list.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a presentational frame for the list.
English turns "He gave Simon the name Peter" into a relative clause.

3:17.sourceText: καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάνην τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Ἰακώβου, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ὄνομα Βοανηργές, ὅ ἐστιν Υἱοὶ Βροντῆς·
3:17.targetText: James son of Zebedee and his brother John (whom He named Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder”),

groups.note: τοῦ Ἰακώβου, "of James", is rendered his.
ἐπέθηκεν … ὄνομα, "put a name on", is rendered named.
αὐτοῖς, "on them", becomes the relative whom.
ὅ ἐστιν, "which is", introduces the translation of the name.

unmappedSource.reason: English lists James without a separate and.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB puts the naming in a relative clause, so this καί has no English word.

3:18.sourceText: καὶ Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖον καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν Καναναῖον
3:18.targetText: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,

unmappedSource.reason: English lists the names with commas, so these καί have no separate English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:19.sourceText: καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριώθ, ὃς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτόν.
3:19.targetText: and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.

groups.note: αὐτόν, "him", is rendered with the name Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί ("also") is not separately expressed in this English wording.

3:20.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς οἶκον· καὶ συνέρχεται πάλιν ὁ ὄχλος, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς μηδὲ ἄρτον φαγεῖν.
3:20.targetText: Then Jesus went home, and once again a crowd gathered, so that He and His disciples could not even eat.

groups.note: εἰς οἶκον, "into a house", is rendered home.
αὐτούς, "they", is spelled out as He and His disciples.
ἄρτον φαγεῖν, "to eat bread", means to have a meal.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

3:21.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆλθον κρατῆσαι αὐτόν· ἔλεγον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξέστη.
3:21.targetText: When His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him, saying, “He is out of His mind.”

groups.note: οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ, "those from Him", means His family.

targetPhrases.text: He is out of His mind

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB renders "for they were saying" as the participle saying, so γάρ has no English word.
The recitative ὅτι marks direct speech and has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English gives heard an object that the Greek participle lacks.

3:22.sourceText: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβάντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Βεελζεβοὺλ ἔχει, καὶ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
3:22.targetText: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons.”

groups.note: The article οἱ with the participle καταβάντες is rendered who had come down.

unmappedSource.reason: The recitative ὅτι marks direct speech and has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:23.sourceText: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Πῶς δύναται Σατανᾶς Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλειν;
3:23.targetText: So Jesus called them together and began to speak to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek participle implies.
English coordinator; the participle προσκαλεσάμενος is rendered as the finite verb called.

3:24.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δύναται σταθῆναι ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη·
3:24.targetText: If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

groups.note: οὐ δύναται, "is not able", is rendered cannot.
ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη, "that kingdom", is resumed as it.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

3:25.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν οἰκία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δυνήσεται ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη στῆναι.
3:25.targetText: If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

groups.note: οὐ δυνήσεται, "will not be able", is rendered cannot.
ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη, "that house", is resumed as it.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

3:26.sourceText: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἀνέστη ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἐμερίσθη, οὐ δύναται στῆναι ἀλλὰ τέλος ἔχει.
3:26.targetText: And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come.

groups.note: οὐ δύναται, "he is not able", is rendered he cannot.
τέλος ἔχει, "he has an end", is rendered his end has come.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB uses a semicolon instead of rendering ἀλλά ("but").

3:27.sourceText: ἀλλ’ οὐ δύναται οὐδεὶς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ εἰσελθὼν τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ διαρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον τὸν ἰσχυρὸν δήσῃ, καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει.
3:27.targetText: Indeed, no one can enter a strong man’s house to steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.

groups.note: Greek doubles the negative (οὐ … οὐδείς); English says no one once.
εἰσελθών with εἰς, "having entered into", is rendered enter.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
English starts a new sentence with Then (τότε), so καί has no separate English word.

3:28.sourceText: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πάντα ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, τὰ ἁμαρτήματα καὶ αἱ βλασφημίαι, ὅσα ἐὰν βλασφημήσωσιν·
3:28.targetText: Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter.

groups.note: ὅσα ἐάν, "whatever", is rendered as many as.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι after I tell you is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:29.sourceText: ὃς δ’ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον, οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ἁμαρτήματος.
3:29.targetText: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”

groups.note: οὐκ … εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, "not … forever", is rendered never.
ἔχει ἄφεσιν, "has forgiveness", is rendered as a passive verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB uses a semicolon instead of rendering ἀλλά ("but").

3:30.targetText: Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the clause that ὅτι ("because") explains.

3:31.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχονται ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔξω στήκοντες ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτὸν καλοῦντες αὐτόν.
3:31.targetText: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came and stood outside. They sent someone in to summon Him,

groups.note: αὐτοῦ ("His") after each noun is rendered once, by the name Jesus.
πρὸς αὐτόν, "to Him", is rendered in, toward where He was.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the messenger that the Greek leaves understood.

3:32.sourceText: καὶ ἐκάθητο περὶ αὐτὸν ὄχλος, καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαί σου ἔξω ζητοῦσίν σε.
3:32.targetText: and a crowd was sitting around Him. “Look,” He was told, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”

groups.note: The dative αὐτῷ ("to Him") becomes the subject of the English passive.
σου after each noun is rendered once, by Your.

unmappedSource.reason: This καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB follows a text without καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαί σου ("and Your sisters"), which N1904 includes.

3:33.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί;
3:33.targetText: But Jesus replied, “Who are My mother and My brothers?”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … λέγει, "answering, He says", is rendered replied.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressee αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker that the Greek verb ending implies.
N1904 has no μου after ἀδελφοί; BSB's second My matches the reading οἱ ἀδελφοί μου.

3:34.sourceText: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος τοὺς περὶ αὐτὸν κύκλῳ καθημένους λέγει Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου.
3:34.targetText: Looking at those seated in a circle around Him, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!

groups.note: The article τούς with the participle καθημένους is rendered those seated.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:35.sourceText: ὃς ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ, οὗτος ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
3:35.targetText: For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The resumptive οὗτος ("this one") is not repeated in English; whoever is the subject of is.

unmappedTarget.reason: N1904 has no γάρ here; BSB's For matches the reading ὃς γὰρ ἄν.
